sourceRecords.title: Constitution of the State of Florida, Article VII, Section 5, Estate, inheritance and income taxes
sourceRecords.retrievalNote: Retrieved in the implementation session. Subsection (a), NATURAL PERSONS, reads in full: No tax upon estates or inheritances or upon the income of natural persons who are residents or citizens of the state shall be levied by the state, or under its authority, in excess of the aggregate of amounts which may be allowed to be credited upon or deducted from any similar tax levied by the United States or any state. Subsection (b), OTHERS, separately permits a tax upon the income of residents and citizens other than natural persons, which is the distinction this pack relies on. This document states a PROHIBITION on the state; it does not state a rate of zero, and no rate is derived from it. publishedAt records the November 5, 1968 ratification of the revised constitution that the retrieved document states in its own preamble; the section's history line records a 1971 amendment whose exact adoption day the retrieved document does not state, so no more precise date is recorded.

sourceRecords.title: Taxes and Fees or Refunds
sourceRecords.retrievalNote: Retrieved in the implementation session. The page is the department's own index of every tax and fee it administers. Its list reads: Communications Services, Corporate Income, Discretionary Sales Surtax, Documentary Stamp, Estate, Fuel, Governmental Leasehold, Gross Receipts Tax on Dry-Cleaning Facilities, Gross Receipts Tax on Utility Services, Insurance Premium, Lead-Acid Battery Fee, Motor Vehicle Warranty Fee, New Tire Fee, Nonrecurring Intangible, Prepaid Wireless Fee, Reemployment, Refunds, Rental Car Surcharge, Sales and Use, Secondhand Dealers and Secondary Metals Recyclers, and Severance. Corporate Income appears and no individual income tax appears anywhere in it. This is the departmental absence, and it is recorded as an absence of an administered tax rather than as a rate. The retrieved page states no publication date, so publishedAt records the session retrieval date and is disclosed here as such rather than presented as a stated publication date.

supportedFeatures.label: No individual income tax imposed
supportedFeatures.reason: The pack states that this jurisdiction imposes no individual income tax, carries the two authorities that establish the absence, and produces a valued record of zero carrying that citation rather than a blank, a dash or an unattributed zero.

unsupportedFeatures.label: Corporate income tax
unsupportedFeatures.reason: The Florida Department of Revenue's administered-tax index lists Corporate Income, and Article VII, Section 5(b) separately addresses residents and citizens other than natural persons. That tax is outside this pack's individual income-tax program.
unsupportedFeatures.successorFeature: A corporate rule pack carrying the corporate rate and base.

unsupportedFeatures.label: Sales and use tax
unsupportedFeatures.reason: The department's administered-tax index lists Sales and Use tax. A consumption tax is outside this pack's income-tax program and this pack carries none of its rates or bases.
unsupportedFeatures.successorFeature: A consumption-tax feature carrying the state rate and the discretionary county surtaxes.

unsupportedFeatures.label: County and municipal taxes
unsupportedFeatures.reason: The department's index lists a Discretionary Sales Surtax levied at county option. No local levy of any kind is carried by this pack, so a household in this jurisdiction is not told its total local burden is zero.
unsupportedFeatures.successorFeature: A local rule pack resolved by county, with its own settlement.

unsupportedFeatures.label: Documentary stamp and nonrecurring intangible taxes
unsupportedFeatures.reason: The department's index lists Documentary Stamp and Nonrecurring Intangible taxes. Both are transaction taxes outside this pack's income-tax program.
unsupportedFeatures.successorFeature: A transaction-tax feature carrying the documentary stamp and nonrecurring intangible rates.

expiryPolicy.reason: The constitutional prohibition and the departmental administered-tax index must both be re-retrieved before this pack is carried past the tax year it declares. An absence established in one year is not evidence of an absence in the next.

noTaxAuthority.locator: Article VII, Section 5, Estate, inheritance and income taxes, subsection (a), NATURAL PERSONS
noTaxAuthority.reason: Two retrieved authorities together establish that no individual income tax reaches this household, and neither of them states a rate. The state constitution prohibits the state, or any authority under it, from levying a tax upon the income of natural persons who are residents or citizens of the state in excess of the aggregate of amounts allowed to be credited upon or deducted from a similar tax levied by the United States or any state, while separately permitting such a tax on residents and citizens other than natural persons. The Florida Department of Revenue's own index of every tax and fee it administers lists Corporate Income and lists no individual income tax. The prohibition plus the departmental absence is what this record states; a zero-percent rate table is not, and none is carried.
